探索：让演员更自发、更有反应
Keith Johnstone, Impro, Routledge 2012 · 目录 · 谷歌图书预览
“In reality status transactions continue all the time.”
在现实中，地位交易一直都在进行。
冲突之外 · 照常进行
反驳朋友之间不玩地位
“My answer is that acquaintances become friends when they agree to play status games together.”
我的回答是：熟人同意一起玩地位游戏的时候，就成了朋友。
“Don’t bite me, I’m not worth the trouble.”
别咬我，我不值得你费劲。
“My belief (at this moment) is that people have a preferred status; that they like to be low, or high, and that they try to manoeuvre themselves into the preferred positions.”
我（此刻）的看法是，人有自己偏爱的地位：他们喜欢低，或者喜欢高，并且会设法让自己挪到偏爱的位置上。
“You become a status specialist, very good at playing one status, but not very happy or competent at playing the other.”
你成了一个地位专才，很擅长演一种地位，演另一种时却不太自在，也不太胜任。
“Finally I explain that I’m keeping my head still whenever I speak, and that this produces great changes in the way I perceive myself and am perceived by others.”
最后我解释说，我每次说话都让头保持不动，这会大大改变我怎么看自己，也大大改变别人怎么看我。
随之自动出现的高地位行为
“Actors needing authority—tragic heroes and so on—have to learn this still head trick. You can talk and waggle your head about if you play the gravedigger, but not if you play Hamlet.”
需要权威的演员——悲剧英雄之类——得学会这个头不动的诀窍。
演掘墓人，你可以边说边晃脑袋；演哈姆雷特就不行。

“… keeping your head still while talking is high status, whereas moving your head side to side a lot is low status. Standing tall with your hands showing is high status, slouching with your hands in your pocket is low status.”
……说话时头不动是高地位，头左右乱晃是低地位。
站得笔直、露出双手是高地位；弓着背、手插在口袋里是低地位。
Nabeel Qureshi, Reflections on Palantir, 2024 · Keith Johnstone, Impro, Routledge 2012, pp. 42–44
“I insist that they have to get their status just a little above or below their partner’s. This ensures that they really ‘see’ their partner …”
我坚持要他们把自己的地位定得只比搭档高一点或低一点。这样能确保他们真正“看见”搭档……
“These status exercises reproduce on the stage exactly the effects of real life, in which moment by moment each person adjusts his status up or down a fraction.”
这些地位练习在舞台上原样再现了现实生活的效果：在现实中，每个人时时刻刻都在把自己的地位往上或往下调一点点。
“The automatic status skills then ‘lock on to’ the other actor, and the students are transformed into observant, and apparently very experienced improvisers.”
自动起作用的地位技巧会“锁定”对方演员，
学生们也就变成了善于观察、看上去经验十足的即兴演员。
“Without the status work my improvisation group, the Theatre Machine, could never have toured successfully in Europe; not without preparing the scenes first.”
没有地位训练，我的即兴剧团 Theatre Machine 绝不可能在欧洲巡演成功；除非事先把场景排好。
“Some students prefer to yield (these are ‘charming’ people) but most prefer to block, even though they may have no idea …”
有些学生喜欢让步（这些是“讨人喜欢”的人），但大多数学生喜欢阻挡，尽管他们可能并不知道……
“I tell my actors never to think up an offer, but instead to assume that one has already been made.”
我告诉我的演员，永远不要去构想提议，而要假定对方已经给出了一个。
“Such disagreements indicate the difficulty of actually perceiving status transactions.”
这类分歧表明，要真正察觉地位交易是困难的。
“… however willing the student is consciously, there may be very strong subconscious resistances. Making the student safe, and getting him to have confidence in you, are essential.”
……无论学生在意识上多么愿意，潜意识里都可能有很强的抵触。让学生感到安全，让他对你有信心，是必不可少的。
Keith Johnstone, Impro, Routledge 2012, p. 99 · Guy MacPherson, Georgia Straight, 2007
“… everything looks prearranged. This is because they accept all offers made—which is something no ‘normal’ person would do. Also they may accept offers which weren’t really intended.”
……一切看上去都像事先安排好的。
这是因为他们接受对方给出的所有提议——
这是任何“正常”人都不会做的事。
他们还可能接受对方其实并非有意给出的提议。
Georgia Straight 电话采访谈接受所有提议这条规则
“… perversion. I think it’s terrible. Bad things have happened to improvisation.”
……扭曲。我觉得这很糟。即兴已经出了些坏事。
对外用法 · 面向客户
Palantir 全球商务负责人 · 对内用法
Ted Mabrey, Commentary on The Technological Republic, 2025 · Stratechery, 2023
“At Palantir, we are taught we should view status as an attribute to use to advance a given situation, not an intrinsic property to define a person.”
我们被教导把地位看作一种属性，
而不是界定一个人的固有特质。
“… something one does. You may be low in social status, but play high, and vice versa.”
……一个人所做的事。你的社会地位可能低，却演高地位，反过来也一样。
